Agenda Item #4
  Meeting Date: April 12, 2022

  MINUTES
  OF THE MARCH 10, 2022 REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates City Council was held via Zoom
videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to AB
361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s recommended measures to
promote social distancing. Members of the public were provided with the following
information to provide public input:

 BYCOMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86156178569
 Zoom Meeting ID: 861 5617 8569
 BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code: 861 5617 8569#

 CALL TO ORDER The meeting was called to order at 6:31 pm.

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE ROLL CALL Due to the format of the meeting the pledge of
 allegiance was not recited.

 Present: Committee Members Rossick, Nye, Vice-Chair Cooper, Chair McCabe.
 Member Rhodes arrived at 6:35 pm

 Also present: City Manager Prestwich, Interim Public Works Director Chankin, Urban
 Forester Moritz.

 APPROVAL OF AGENDA The Committee Members concurred to approve the Agenda as
 presented.

 INTRODUCTION: The Chair introduced City Manager Mark Prestwich who greeted the
 Committee Members stating he was looking forward to meeting them in person and working
 with the Committee this year. He thanked them for their volunteer work.

 Parklands Committee Minutes
 March 10, 2022
 COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Tom Bechler addressed the Committee.

CITIZEN APPLICATIONS

1. PC-562-22: APPLICATION TO REMOVE ONE FICUS TREE LOCATED IN THE
  PARKWAY BEHIND AND ADJACENT TO 705 MEXICO PLACE AND PLANT
  STREET TREES AND SHRUBS IN THE RIGHT-OF-WAY ADJACENT TO PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE WEST

  APPLICANT: BEN O’ROUKE, 4040 VIA SOLANO, PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CA
  90274

  Urban Forester Moritz presented the staff report indicating the applicant was requesting
  the removal of one Fichus tree adjacent to and behind 705 Mexico Place and to plant
  street trees and shrubs in the right-of-way adjacent to Palos Verdes Drive West. The
  designated street tree for Palos Verdes Drive West was the Peruvian Pepper tree. He
  presented photographs of the house and the area where the tree was located, noting It
  was very close to the property line. He provided a list of reasons for the application
  including view enhancement.  Urban Forester Moritz stated the tree was out of
  character with the area as an additional reason for removal. Even though it was a view
  application, it was mostly to build a property line wall since most of the trees were gone
  and the view was not really affected.

  Urban Forester Moritz described the condition of the tree noting that the tree was healthy
  but has never been maintained and has grown into the hedge adjacent to 701 Mexico
  Place when it was one lot. The City has not received any opposition or support, but has
  received late correspondence from Mr. Briggs expressing concern about the payment
  to the street tree bank. He advised the Committee of what needed to be considered for
  view related applications. He advised that the application requested the removal of two
  trees, however, the Alder tree was not included because it was dead and it was not
  necessary to get permission to remove it. It would be removed when the fire safety
  crews reached that location.

  Urban Forester Moritz provided background on the Fichus tree noting it was growing in
  the parkway of the street right-of way, adjacent to Palos Verdes Drive West on or very
  close to the property line. The home has not been constructed so it would be difficult to
  say what the view impacts would be or how the view would be enhanced by its removal.
  The tree was one of three in a row adjacent to the lot at 705 Mexico Place. The Palos
  Verdes Homes Association provided approval for these trees to be removed based on
  the Fire Department’s specifications as a major problem for fire distance and roof
  structures. He discussed the tree not being in character with the neighborhood and the
  privacy for 705 Mexico Place, adding that planting new street trees adjacent to the
  parkway of Palos Verdes Drive West would provide privacy and screening for 705
  Mexico Place from Palos Verdes Drive West as the trees mature. The applicant was

Parklands Committee Minutes
March 10, 2022
   requesting to plant three new Peppers and 16 native California shrubs.

  The Urban Forester added that the applicant didn’t need permission to plant the Pepper
  trees and shrubs because it was public right-of-way and went through the Neighborhood
  Compatibility to meet the requirements for the planting of street trees in the right of way
  and Parklands. Urban Forester Moritz informed the Committee of the City’s prohibition
  of planting Fichus trees and the fire hazards. Staff recommended the removal of the
  Fichus tree located in the parkway adjacent to and behind 705 Mexico Place according
  to standard conditions for tree removal approvals and staff was recommending the
  requirement of a $500 payment to the tree bank and a tree removal permit for removal
  of the stump. He advised the Committee they had the discretion to waive the tree bank
  payment since the tree was not a designated street tree.

  Thereafter the Committee asked questions regarding the planting of three street trees
  to which the Urban Forester clarified that the area requested by the applicant was street
  right-of-way and not Parklands. As a result, the applicant has the responsibility when
  going through the Neighborhood Compatibility to provide for trees which would screen
  structures and be far enough away not to be a fire hazard. Mr. Moritz confirmed that
  the Committee could make it part of their recommendation to plant three Pepper trees
  in the right-of-way. The Urban Forester also addressed the Committee’s concern about
  erosion onto the street explaining that the applicant’s plan included 16 native plants and
  three trees which would put roots into the soil as well as the remaining Bougainvillea.
  He explained that it was within the Committee’s jurisdiction to condition the plantings.
  Urban Forester Moritz explained the concerns Mr. Briggs expressed in his
  correspondence on this issue. A lengthy discussion ensued regarding the removal of
  the Fichus tree, the replacement with three street trees, and the committee’s discretion
  to not require payment in to the tree bank.

  Deborah Richie Bray, the landscape architect for the applicant addressed the Committee
  explaining this was not a view application but rather approval to remove the tree to put
  in a property line wall. It has to do with safety, security and privacy for the owners and
  the Fichus doesn’t really belong in this area. Ms. Richie-Bray advised that with the
  removal of the tree, the applicant wanted to add a new property line wall; however, when
  the survey was prepared, the tree was on the right-of-way line and not on the owner’s
  property. Ms. Richie-Bray advised that the trees to be planted are the designated street
  trees. She concluded by stating the applicant would be adding 11 new shrubs and three
  larger Pepper trees.

  The following individuals addressed the Committee:
  Don Briggs
  Laura Agnew
  John Weick

  ACTION: Moved by Vice-Chair Cooper, and seconded by Committee Member Nye, to
  grant the application to remove the fichus tree, waive the $500 payment to the tree bank,
  and adopt the Applicant’s plan to plant the three Pepper trees, the shrubbery as outlined

Parklands Committee Minutes
March 10, 2022
   by the Applicant’s representative, and the requirement that the Applicant water the trees
  for two years. The motion unanimously carried by the following roll call vote:
  AYES: Rossick, Nye, Rhodes, Cooper, McCabe
  NOES: None

2. PC-CTP-13-21: CONCEPT PLAN TO ENHANCE THE PARKLANDS
  SURROUNDING GEORGE ALLEN BASEBALL FIELD

  APPLICANT: GEORGE ALLEN NEIGHBORS ASSOCIATION-GHAZALA KAHN,
  1512 VIA LOPEZ, PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CA 90274

  Urban Forester Moritz presented a PowerPoint and provided a staff report indicating
  the George Allen Neighbors Association request consideration of the concept plan to
  George Allen Field pursuant to the Parklands Use Policy and the Change to Parkland’s
  Application Guidelines. Mr. Moritz presented a PowerPoint and reminded the
  Committee that at the May 13, 2021 Parklands Committee meeting, the Parklands Plan
  for George Allen Field was submitted and the Committee supported the concept and
  provided additional concepts to consider which included an additional baseball field or
  soccer field and agreed the project should be developed further based on the Parklands
  Committee’s discussion. The Urban Forester described the preliminary design that was
  reviewed in the initial concept plan submitted at the May 13, 2021, Committee meeting.

  The new concept plan included an acre of native grass around the baseball field, a
  6,277 square foot bio swell, a 30 space parking lot, and a parking spot for a food truck
  and porta-potty. The new parking lot road would be one-way, 12 feet wide, and road
  base is being proposed. Careful boulder placement in this area to create traffic barriers
  was also being proposed. The bio swell in the center of the parking lot was intended to
  direct rainwater runoff from the parking lot to a depression designed to capture, treat
  and infiltrate storm water as it flowed downhill to the storm drain system in the street.
  Approximately one acre of native turf grass was being proposed around the perimeter
  of the baseball fence. This would require less water than typical ornamental church
  grass lawn but would still be a considerable monthly bill if irrigated all year long. It was
  not clear if the intent was to let it go brown and uncut with no irrigation.

  Urban Forester Moritz showed a picture of what the field looked like today. The George
  Allen Neighbors Association has requested to phase the project. The previously
  submitted concept for a perimeter trail in native plantings would be in a future phase.
  Approval of the current concept plan was necessary to develop the project further so a
  complete proposed plan for the entire area could be considered for a final plan. The
  application considered on May 13, 2021 requested the City contribute boulders, rocks,
  mulch, and water allocation. Providing boulders and edging rocks has been provided
  for other projects and has not been a problem. The City always generates mulch and
  currently generating a lot of mulch right now with the fire safety contract.

  Payment of the water bill has not been required of other applicants and would be a cost
  to the City unless other conditions were recommended by the Parklands Committee.

Parklands Committee Minutes
March 10, 2022
   Staff believed a new water meter should be added to separate the baseball field usage
  from the passive park so there would be two meters; and a complete watering system
  designed for all the concept areas as required and reviewed in the proposed plan.
  When that was done an estimated cost to the City could be established. It should be
  noted that access to power be considered; staff thought there may be power in the low
  score board to run a controller for a watering system but that would have to be
  something that is confirmed.

  Mr. Moritz advised that a licensing agreement for the maintenance in perpetuity would
  be required. Staff has been advised by the Applicant that the Lunada Bay Homeowners
  Association would be the signatory on the license agreement. The Urban Forester
  noted that the Parklands Use Policy does not address parking lots and staff was not
  aware of any prior approvals of parking in a Parklands Application. Therefore, the
  precedent might be a consideration. This concept plan if approved, would be returned
  to the Parklands Committee as a proposed plan for review and the proposed plan would
  become a final plan upon approval of the City Council, then the project could move
  forward.

  The Parklands Committee was to consider the Parklands Use Policy and the Change
  to Parklands Application Guidelines in review of this concept plan and the Change to
  Parklands Use Policy. The Parklands Committee may consider all factors in
  determining the potential public benefit. Staff recommended the Committee approve
  the concept plan and direct the George Allen Field Neighbors Association to prepare a
  proposed plan that considered all the comments in the staff report and any comments
  the committee may make.

  Urban Forester Moritz responded to questions posed by the committee.

  Interim Public Works Director Chankin responded to questions regarding the license
  agreement with the Little League for use of the field and maintenance.

  Marlene Breene addressed the Committee on behalf of the applicant and presented a
  PowerPoint for the George Allen Field concept plan. She advised the neighbors wanted
  to mitigate some issues that the site has and make it more attractive. She described
  the road base noting it was permeable and not as permanent as an asphalt parking
  area and it blended with the natural look of the park. The green area around the
  baseball diamond was requested by the Junior League as a buffer area for balls hit
  outside the diamond. The applicants estimated 30 parking spaces because that would
  be the number of people that would want to park for a typical game. She explained the
  impact if the parking lot was not approved. Ms. Breene addressed the water issue and
  felt it would not take that much water stating it would be controllable. She advised the
  Palos Verdes Estates Foundation has already received donations between $15,000
  and $20,000 to help move the project forward so the community was definitely vested
  in what’s being proposed. More discussion with the City would be required regarding
  the license agreement. She noted the trail around the exterior was from the first
  presentation which they would like keep and noted the parking area would be in the

Parklands Committee Minutes
March 10, 2022
   first phase and the trail would be in Phase Two. She indicated everything depended
  on funding and what’s approved. Ms. Breene concluded by showing some examples
  of the native plants that will be planted.

  In response to the Committee Members’ questions about continued support and
  maintenance costs, Ms. Breene explained that a garden club would be formed so
  anyone can be a part of the club. The Palos Verdes Foundation has been set up for
  funding so anyone can donate and it would be tax deductible through the Foundation.
  She also indicated that areas of the project were eligible for grant funding. She
  continued discussing volunteers and maintenance of the area.

  Damien Cappazola, Board Member of the Peninsula Junior League addressed the
  Committee regarding the proposed plan for the baseball field.

  Chris Sorebia, Conservation Director for the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land
  Conservancy discussed the project and the positive aspects of the native plants and
  the bio swell to be used. He felt if this project was approved it would be very successful
  and beneficial to the flora and fauna.

  Kevin Piper addressed the Committee and presented a PowerPoint of the grass and
  native plants that were being proposed. He provided details on the native plants and
  sod that was being proposed. He also showed a slide of what road base looked like
  and described the texture and mixture of road base.

  The Committee discussed the issue and expressed their gratitude and appreciation for
  the project. In response to questions about the phasing of the project and what decision
  was being sought this evening, Ms. Breene informed the Committee that they were
  looking at starting with the parking lot and approval of the concept plan.

  A lengthy discussion ensued regarding the details of the project, the next steps for the
  project and what the Committee needed to do. The Committee asked about adding
  some trees for shade for the spectators during games. Committee Member Nye
  suggested that the participation for this endeavor and the ongoing funding be
  emphasized clearly when brought back. Ms. Breene advised that the Lunada Bay
  Homeowners Association was in support of the project

  ACTION: Moved by Committee Member Rhodes, and seconded by Vice Chair Copper,
  to move forward with Phase 1 of the concept plan so a final plan could be presented.
  The motion unanimously carried by the following roll call vote:
  AYES: Rossick, Nye, Rhodes, Cooper, McCabe
  NOES: None

ITEMS OF INFORMATION FROM THE COMMITTEE/STAFF

3. FOLLOW UP DISCUSSION TO THE CITY COUNCIL PARKLANDS WORKSHOP OF
  SEPTEMBER 14, 2021

Parklands Committee Minutes
March 10, 2022
   Chair McCabe stated at the joint meeting with the City Council in September what
  seemed to be the most pressing item from that meeting was preparation of a tree
  inventory and a tree management plan and policy. Chair McCabe discussed forming a
  separate committee to look at tree management policies of cities similar to Palos Verdes
  Estates and incorporating what’s in those policies into the City’s policy.

  The Committee discussed the significance of a tree inventory and the fact that the City
  has set funds aside for an inventory.

  The Committee discussed appointing a sub-committee to deal with the Tree
  Management Policy and Plan. The Committee members concurred to establish sub-
  committees. Further discussion ensued regarding Parklands issues not being
  communicated to the Committee, that the members felt they should be made aware of,
  such as the Fire Safety Weed Abatement project and parklands maintenance. There
  was a feeling by some committee members that their responsibilities as a committee be
  made a little more clear.

  Mr. McCabe discussed the issue of Parklands encroachments which was discussed at
  the Joint Meeting.

  Interim Public Works Director Chankin advised that the City now has a fulltime Code
  Enforcement Officer and a sub-committee in that area could be fruitful.

  A lengthy discussion continued regarding the Committee’s duties, the limited number of
  staff to get things done, and the lack of information being brought to the Committee for
  their information and discussion.

  The following individuals addressed the Committee:
  Don Briggs
  Marlene Breene

  The Committee concurred that Item 3 has been accomplished and staff would work with
  the Committee to take a broader view of its duties of providing data to the Committee to
  consider on an ongoing basis and work collaboratively on the big picture.

  The Committee moved the report on Citywide Fire Safety Weed Abatement Contract
  before Item 4.

  UPDATE ON CITYWIDE FIRE SAFETY WEED ABATEMENT CONTRACT

  Interim Public Works Director provided an update on the Fire Safety Weed Abatement
  Contract by providing a background of the contract with Oakridge Landscape and the
  abatement within 100 feet from the property line. As part of this abatement, trees were
  being removed under the direction of the Urban Forester to mitigate any fire hazards.
  She offered the committee members a chance to make an appointment with the Urban

Parklands Committee Minutes
March 10, 2022
   Forester to tour the fire safety weed abatement area so they have an opportunity to
  observe. Ms. Chankin discussed the new Code Enforcement Officer who was working
  with the Urban Forester to learn the areas that have been encroached and she is
  beginning to build a file on encroachments. Committee Member Rhodes advised that
  there was an encroachment inventory with photographs and addresses previously
  completed.

  Chairman McCabe asked that Items 3, 4, and 5 be placed on the Agenda for each
  meeting going forward.

4. DISCUSSION AND PRIORITIZATION OF POTENTIAL FOLLOW UP STEPS TO THE
  CITY COUNCIL PARKLANDS WORKSHOP OF SEPTEMBER 14, 2021

  Recommendation: Consider appointment of an ad hoc subcommittee and/or provide
  direction to staff.

  The Committee formed two sub-committees and made the following appointments:
  Encroachment Sub-Committee:
  Robert Cooper
  Susie Rossick

  Tree Inventory and Management Policy and Plan Sub-Committee:
  Paul McCabe
  Kim Rhodes

  Chair McCabe made it clear that the sub-committees were going to review the
  information from the Joint Meeting with Council and anything that has transpired since
  then, and come up with an action plan for the next meeting in May.

  Chair McCabe also asked that an information item be added to the agendas so if any
  member wants to discuss an issue or request a future agenda item they can do so.

ADJOURNMENT

  ACTION: Moved by Committee Member Rhodes, and seconded by Vice-Chair Cooper
  to adjourn the meeting to the Regular Meeting of May 12, 2022 at 6:30 pm.

Respectfully submitted,

_____________________________
Carol Cowley
